_comment: One job per STRIP — the whole strip as one image, for the concept run. Run with comic_render.py --provider runway|google|openai.

jobs.title: The postcard
jobs.prompt: a four-panel newspaper comic strip, four equal panels in a single horizontal row with thin black gutters (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 19, thin young man with a slouch, three days' stubble, hair longer, brown canvas chore coat with a frayed cuff and one mismatched button, hands always in its pockets; BARNABY (the dog) — a low-slung terrier and hound mix, long body, short legs, folded velvet ears, wiry white-and-tan coat, gray on the muzzle from 2004, cloudy eyes from 2009, carried from 2010. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: A postcard from Seattle in tiny manic handwriting. Wood reads it aloud to the dog. He edits. Panel 1: a young man at a bedroom drawing table reading a postcard of a needle-shaped tower aloud, a scruffy dog under the table with one ear up, brush-pen black and white (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Wood says "Listen to this. 'Wood — there is a gallery here that only shows things made of light.'". Panel 2: close-up of the back of a postcard covered edge to edge in tiny cramped manic handwriting, a thumb covering one corner. No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: a young man reading a postcard and visibly skipping lines while a dog under the table lowers its ear (in this panel: WOOD, BARNABY (the dog)). Wood says "'...guerrilla theater in a parking garage...' — skip — '...you'd hate it, you'd love hating it...' — skip —". Panel 4: close-up of a hand pinning a postcard to a corkboard with its photo side facing out and its written side to the wall, no words (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized crab, seen from above. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @barnaby is the model sheet for BARNABY (the dog): match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23; @barnaby for the character Barnaby; @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17.
